doc: Node facts, goals, fit constants and experiments for the Magpie planner. Rules apply in file order (general first, later rules override key by key; args/drop accumulate). A rule applies when all when_all tags are present, any when_any tag is present (if given), no unless_any tag is present, no exceptions entry (a list of tags that must all be present) matches, and - if it names an experiment - that experiment is enabled. Keys: set = fixed-param values; env = child env defaults (real env wins, null = force unset); fit = memory/speed model constants; allow/deny = candidate filters per tuned param; args = extra llama-server CLI args; drop = params NOT passed to llama-server (left to llama.cpp's own defaults); payload = fields merged into every request sent to llama-server; features = supervisor behaviour switches (ring_restore, ring_autosave, stall_s). Tuned params have no default bound: default null means the search uses the full range. fault_backoff_at = after this many GPU faults of one model with the same kv/fa/experiment key, that model's GPU budget is capped fit.bad_margin_gb under the faulting plan's GPU estimate, like a memory failure (0 = off: faults are only counted).

tool_calls.what: passes --jinja so OpenAI-style tools / tool_calls work (needed by the code agent). Recent llama.cpp builds may already default to jinja; the flag is then a no-op.

mtp_spec.status: working on gfx1103 + Qwen3.8-27B MTP (2-7 t/s, avg 4-5); stability not tied to it in testing
mtp_spec.what: self-speculative decoding using the model's own MTP (nextn) heads. Only applies to models tagged mtp. The draft context is a second context with its own KV cache for the full -c and its own compute buffers; its KV type is --cache-type-k/v-draft (llama.cpp default f16, so this rule asks for q8_0).
mtp_spec.open: draft-context memory is unmeasured: fit.gpu_extra_gb 1.5 assumes one q8_0 KV layer at about 190K context plus its compute buffer (it was 0.5, which one f16 KV layer at that context can already exceed). Replace it with the draft context's KV and compute buffer sizes from the load log once known. Flag names come from the llama.cpp build in use - if the server refuses to start with it on, the build does not know them

no_reuse.what: turns off prompt-prefix reuse (cache_prompt=false) plus ring restore/autosave. Tests whether GPU hangs on hybrid (recurrent+attention) models come from reusing saved/cached state - both observed hangs happened right after a restore or a partial-prefix reuse.
no_reuse.open: if hangs stop with this on, the next step is narrowing to restore-only vs prefix-reuse-only

llama_fit.what: stops passing -ngl so llama.cpp's own fit (common_fit_params) picks GPU layers against free device memory; the planner still chooses ctx/kv/ubatch.
llama_fit.open: compare its chosen layer count (in the load log) with the planner's est.ngl to calibrate the fit constants

unified_unset.status: mechanism verified in source, effect on nodes untested
unified_unset.what: removes GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY from the child env entirely - the only way to turn managed memory off. ggml-cuda decides with getenv("GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY") != nullptr, so any value, 0 included, turns it on; the rules therefore write 1.
unified_unset.open: with this on, GPU buffers come from the BIOS carve only: a 4 GB-carve node cannot offload past it, a 16 GB-carve node keeps its buffers in the carve instead of system RAM

no_op_offload.what: passes --no-op-offload: during prompt processing (batches of 32+ tokens) llama.cpp normally copies the weights of CPU-resident layers to the GPU and runs those matmuls there; with this on they run on the CPU. Tests whether hangs that happen mid-prefill come from that traffic.
no_op_offload.open: prefill gets slower when many layers are on the CPU; token generation is unchanged

host_cache_cap.what: bounds llama-server's own host-RAM caches and counts them in the memory model (fit.host_cache_gb): turns off the prompt cache (--cache-ram, llama.cpp default 8192 MiB of saved conversation states) and keeps 8 context checkpoints per slot for hybrid/SWA models (--ctx-checkpoints, default 32). Neither was counted, and the planner fills RAM to within reserve_gb. A conversation still reuses its own prefix in the slot; only switching between long conversations re-processes the prompt.
host_cache_cap.open: host_cache_gb 0.9 assumes about 100 MiB per checkpoint; the real size depends on the model (the server logs a line with 'context checkpoint' and its size). To keep a prompt cache, raise --cache-ram to N MiB and host_cache_gb by N/954 - every GB of it is a GB less KV, so less context. Fewer checkpoints means more re-processing when a conversation's earlier history is edited (the server logs it as 'created context checkpoint N of M ... size = X MiB'); fewer checkpoints means more re-processing when a conversation's history is edited. If the server refuses to start with it on, the build does not know the flags

stall_watchdog.what: kills llama-server and retries if a streaming response produces no line for features.stall_s seconds (a hung-but-alive server).
stall_watchdog.open: prefill of very long prompts sends no lines; stall_s must exceed the longest expected prefill

verbose_load.what: passes -lv 4 so llama.cpp prints per-buffer sizes at load (calibration data for measure()).
verbose_load.open: the exact verbosity level that prints buffer sizes in this build is unverified

spec_draft.what: Speculative decoding using a secondary draft GGUF model (--spec-draft-model). The draft model must share the target model's vocabulary.
spec_draft.open: reserves extra memory for the draft model weights in the planner

no_flash_attn.what: forces --flash-attn off and pins KV to f16 (fa off with a quantized KV is refused by the planner; q4_0+fa is the known-NaN combo on this arch). Flash attention on gfx1103/RDNA3 via ROCm is the most common source of mid-prefill GPU hangs and was hardcoded on for this arch, so it had never been tested off. no_reuse/no_op_offload/stall_watchdog all still hung with fa on.
no_flash_attn.open: f16 KV roughly doubles KV memory so max context drops (expected for the test; LightRAG extraction prompts still fit). If hangs stop with this on, flash attention is the cause - wire it into fault_ladder so a fault backs off to it automatically.

small_batch.what: caps the logical batch (-b) and micro-batch (-ub) to 128 so prompt processing runs in 128-token chunks instead of 1024. The hangs all land during prompt processing of a >1000-token batch; this tests whether the dispatch size is the trigger.
small_batch.open: prefill is slower with a smaller batch. Test each lever alone before combining, so the result stays attributable.

rules.doc: Radeon 760M/780M. Kernels are built for gfx1100, so the override is required. Tested: q4_0 KV + flash attention gives NaN/degenerate output on this arch (q8_0 and f16 are fine); SDMA=0 avoids GTT staging corruption.
Managed (unified) memory on: GPU buffers come from system RAM through the driver, so the GPU can use more than the BIOS carve. Any value enables it (see experiment unified_unset).

16 GB-class BIOS carve: the GPU fits large models without GTT spill. Managed memory stays on here (it was written as 0, which ggml also reads as on); for buffers in the carve itself, set the variable to null in this rule.

4 GB-class carve: offload depends on GTT. Ryzen 7 H 255 / 32 GB / gttsize=28672: gtt_ram_cap 0.8 planned ~22 GB GPU-side and hung at ngl 46; 0.5 (the maintainer's observed 'GPU pool = min(RAM/2, GTT)' ceiling) planned ~15.6 GB, where ngl 39 ran. Raise only with measure() data.
Apple silicon unified memory. vram = GPU wired limit (sudo sysctl iogpu.wired_limit_mb=N). Compute-buffer constants are guesses.

Radeon 760M/780M via Mesa/RADV Vulkan. GPU budget from the device-local carve (gpu_frac) plus the GTT/host-visible heap (gtt_frac) - the same split the hip rules (amd_hip + apu_carve_small) give, which the vulkan tag would otherwise lose, leaving ngl 0 (CPU-only). RADV allocations show in the sysfs VRAM+GTT counters, so no unified-measure flag.
